chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Beware of the children of the rich and the tyrant kings, for their trial (fitnah) is more intense than the trial of the virgins in their private chambers.'
ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the fitnah of the children of the rich and kings?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) warns against the 'fitnah' (trial or temptation) associated with the children of the wealthy and tyrannical kings, describing it as more intense than that of virgins in their private chambers. This comparison highlights the powerful allure of beauty and youth, as well as the potential for social and moral disruption caused by their status and abundance. The hadith is often interpreted in Shia scholarship as referring to the temptation of sodomy, given its placement in the chapter on 'The Sodomy'.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Beware of the children of the rich and the kings, the tyrants, for their strife is more intense than the strife of the virgins in their dens (private chambers)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘You must remain on your guard against the children of the affluent people and the tyrant kings because their mischief is more intense than the mischief of the virgins in their private chambers.’”
